start_here: Say to your AI: "Calibrate a camera's view of a court, table or screen once from four corners, so every later point is measured in that frame", with {"min_confidence":0.8,"detected":{"corners":[[100,50],[500,80],[540,400],[60,380]],"confidence":0.95},"points":[[100,50]]}. It runs tool:calibrate-a-camera-frame and answers {"state":"calibrated","source":"auto","confidence":0.95,"h":[0.002415578823559963,0.0002927974331587834,-0.25619775401393546,-0.0002757098857977818,0.003676131810637091,-0.15623560195207636,-0.0001480900621827622,0.000613256043876624,1],"failures":[],"points":[[0,0]]}
no_lists_because: It names no list of yours: it takes its input and answers, and keeps no row.
instructions: 1. Say to your AI: "Calibrate a camera's view of a court, table or screen once from four corners, so every later point is measured in that frame", and give it min_confidence.
2. The AI calls run_resource_operation at @workshop-tools with method tools:run, tool tool:calibrate-a-camera-frame and its input (the worked example shows one).

3. Read what comes back: Give min_confidence (the floor an automatic result must reach) and detected ({ corners: four [x, y] in the order top-left, top-right, bottom-right, bottom-left, confidence }) as a corner detector gave it, or null; manual_corners (four [x, y] from a guided manual adjustment) are used when the automatic result is missing, too unsure or unusable.
